scenes.name: Nu skool breaks / breakstep
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: Una versión tecnológica del breakbeat combinada con electro, house y hip hop, producto de la diáspora post-hardcore; de su fusión con el 2step nace el breakstep (Stanton Warriors, Zed Bias).
scenes.family: Hip hop, breaks y ritmo lento

podcast.title: The Crow: Salvation Soundtrack Contribution (2000)
podcast.body: The Crystal Method contributed to *The Crow: Salvation* soundtrack, released in the spring of 2000. This album was associated with the sequel to *The Crow: City of Angels*, although the movie itself did not appear until 2004 and went straight to DVD. "More Hole, More Filter, Monster Magnet, Stabbing Westward, Kid Rock, Crystal Method."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Electronic Music Integration
podcast.body: The Crystal Method was identified as an artist that started to produce electronic music sounds as E-Lectronica gained significant traction at the end of the 1990s. "Similarly, electronic music started coming out of Bjork, and Moby, and Underworld, and the Crystal Method, and Daffed Punk, and Air."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock

podcast.title: Inspired to Record Studio Albums
podcast.body: The Crystal Method (implied by "cristal mezo") was among the DJs who, following The Chemical Brothers' lead, were encouraged to enter the recording studio and release their own impactful albums. "justo después del primer disco es chemical brothers vienen los discos de... cristal mezo."

srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT

podcast.title: Summersault Festival International Act
podcast.body: The Crystal Method was an international act included in Our Lady Peace's Summersault Festival lineup in 1998. "That lineup included I'm other Earth, McGandarves, as well as international flavor from Garbage, the Crystal Method and Eve 6."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
